risks: delete must validate the ID before it changes anything. If it called self._tasks.pop(task_id) directly, True would resolve to ID 1.
It must leave _next_id alone. Resetting the counter when the store becomes empty would reuse IDs, and that would break AC-3.

_snapshot and _restore reject a next_id that is not above every stored ID. After deletion next_id may be well above the highest remaining ID, which is allowed. Save and load of an empty store with a high counter must still work, so the existing persistence code should need no change.
Removing a key from the dict keeps the remaining insertion order, so no reordering code is needed. The method must return the same Task object that was stored, not a copy.

A missing ID must raise KeyError after validation passes and before any mutation. Using get() or a pop on a validated ID gives the right errors, but the code must not catch ValueError and turn it into KeyError.
